body.x: 4N Inc. (CEO Seongkyun Kim) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10, as part of the K-Startup Pavilion.

Founded by KAIST-educated bio and brain engineering experts, 4N Inc. leverages brain engineering and AI technology to innovate mental healthcare. Its flagship solution, ‘My Brain Story,’ integrates advanced EEG analysis with explainable AI to assess brain activity, identify abnormal areas, and provide actionable insights for diagnosis and treatment.

4N collaborates with prominent organizations such as Neuin Inc., KAIST, UNIST, Catholic University, Pukyong National University, and the Korean National Police Agency to develop and deliver innovative services. These partnerships aim to revolutionize mental healthcare through AI-driven brainwave analysis, with plans to expand its impact across the industry.

At CES 2025, the company aims to promote ‘My Brain Story’ and seek partners for global expansion. The solution uses EEG data to analyze brain activity, providing detailed information about anomalies in specific brainwave channels. This supports mental health diagnosis and validates the effectiveness of treatment methods.

‘My Brain Story’ features include quantifiable EEG analysis results, insights into brain health issues like depression, anxiety, or hemispheric imbalance, and precise identification of abnormal brain regions. The platform fosters rapport between examiners and patients by offering diagnostic support and clear explanations, encouraging proactive treatment engagement.

One standout feature is its ability to integrate with tools like BDI scores to measure depression levels with over 95% accuracy. Additionally, identifying affected brain regions enhances applications for electronic drugs and neuromodulation therapies. The solution also tracks brain changes post-treatment, verifying therapeutic outcomes.

‘My Brain Story’ provides personalized EEG history analysis, enabling adaptive responses to individual changes. Future developments include partnerships to expand applications for diagnosing ADHD, ASD, AD, and other mental disorders.

While 4N has not yet launched its services overseas, it has a strategic roadmap to enter the U.S. and U.K. markets. The company aims to position itself as a global leader in AI-driven mental health diagnostics.

A company representative stated, “Securing strategic footholds in North America and Europe will allow us to validate our services, drive technological innovation, and refine our offerings. The potential scale and opportunities of these markets will be the foundation for sustainable growth.”

Beyond mental health diagnostics, 4N aspires to expand into broader fields. Future goals include expanding global services, acquiring data, developing technology for diverse mental health applications, and introducing electronic drug and neuromodulation technologies for optimal therapeutic outcomes.
